thread:
alice (support): FYI getting a high-severity escalation from Acme: their /v1/generate calls are returning 5xx from our gateway starting ~10:12 UTC. They report ~25-35% error rate and spike coincides with a heavy batch job.  

acme says errors look like 502 / 504 coming from control-plane deps. Can SRE take a look? :rotating_light:  

jordan (acct): Customer is hitting us in prod-eu, important account, they said this is affecting realtime UX. They're asking for ETA and mitigation.

ben (sre): On it. Can you paste a sample request id and a short curl that reproduces? Also any customer-side logs?

alice (support): Request id from customer's last failed call: req_0a9f3c. Minimal repro curl from them:  
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -d '{"model":"lively-3","input":"hi"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Response snippet:  
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
{ "error": "control_plane_5xx", "detail": "routing policy timeout -> config-db" }
```

ben (sre): Thanks. I'm seeing a spike in control-plane 5xx traces starting 10:11:40 UTC across eu-region. Root traces show timeouts calling routing-policy-service and session-auth (504) and a cascade to gateway which surfaces as 502. Pushing logs:  
```
[10:11:42] routing-policy-service -> ERROR: timeout waiting for configdb (query id=Q_3345)
[10:11:43] session-svc -> WARN: auth lookup timeout (user=acme-cust)
[10:11:44] gateway -> ERROR: control_plane_5xx: child=timeout(routing-policy)
```

configdb-monitor-bot: ALERT: configdb avg p99 latency 4.2s (baseline 120ms) across eu cluster. Connection pool saturation at 92%. Increased read replica lag detected.

carla (eng-runtime): I can take routing-policy + auth traces. Initial hunch: config DB experiencing slow queries causing routing-service to wait on queries (policy resolution) and sessions to block on token lookup. Any recent deploys to config-db or routing?

deploy-bot: deploy: routing-policy-service v1.16.2 rolled at 09:58 UTC to eu-primary (canary -> full). No errors reported during deploy.

ben (sre): Looking at DB slow query log: a new analytics job (internal) started at 10:05 and launched heavy aggregate queries against policies table without index hints. There are repeated full table scans. Example slow query:  
```
SELECT * FROM policies WHERE json_extract(payload, '$.last_updated') > '2026-03-01' LIMIT 1000;
```

carla (eng-runtime): Oof. That explains the db p99 spike and connection pool exhaustion. Routing-policy svc has no circuit breaker for configdb calls, so RPCs block and time out later. Immediate mitigation options:  
- Kill offending analytics job (if internal) or throttle it.
- Temporarily enable routing-policy fallback to default-policy when configdb times out (fast fail).
- Increase configdb connection pool and add a short request timeout for policy lookups.

ben (sre): I'm contacting infra team to throttle/stop the analytics job. Oncall-manager (ops) can you approve kill?

oncall-manager (ops): Approved. We halted the analytics job at 10:18 UTC. Noted: job owner is data-eng; I'll follow up.

carla (eng-runtime): While job was stopped, I patched routing-policy-service to add a short 300ms timeout to configdb lookups and a fallback path to default routing policy for timeouts. Pushing hotfix to eu cluster now.

deploy-bot: rolling restart routing-policy-service eu-primary: started 10:21 UTC -> 10:27 UTC (3/3 pods restarted).

ben (sre): After the restart and stopping the analytics job I see configdb p99 drop to ~150ms and control-plane 5xx rate fall to near-zero by 10:28 UTC. Acme reports success on retries.

alice (support): Customer updated: they've retried and errors are gone for them. They're asking what happened and whether this will reoccur. I told them we're investigating root cause and will share mitigation + steps.

carla (eng-runtime): Root cause: unbounded analytics query caused config DB latency spike and connection pool saturation -> routing-policy blocked -> auth/session lookups delayed -> gateway surfaced control-plane 5xx. Permanent fix items:  
- Add DB indexes and optimize the offending analytics query (assigned to data-eng).
- Add circuit breaker + short read timeouts in routing-policy and session services (eng-runtime).
- Increase DB read replica capacity and set query concurrency limits (infra).
- Add proactive alerting for configdb connpool saturation and slow queries (sre + infra).

ben (sre): Immediate post-incident mitigation already applied: stopped job, rolled restart with timeout fallback. Long term actions noted. Assigning follow-ups in tracker.

oncall-manager (ops): Severity P2 -> moving to P1 during active outage window. Postmortem requested. Owner: carla (eng-runtime). Data-eng owner: matt (data-eng). SLO impact: small but visible for customers in eu for ~16 minutes.

jordan (acct): I'm coordinating an incident email to Acme summarizing impact and remediation. Please include timeline and the mitigation we applied + next steps. I'll offer a small credit for the disruption.

alice (support): Thanks team. I'll close the realtime support escalation once the email is sent. Action items:  
- carla: postmortem + code changes for circuit breaker (due EOD).
- matt (data-eng): fix analytics query + add indexes (blocker for reoccurrence).
- infra: scale read replicas and add connection pool alert (1-2d).
- ben: create runbook entry for routing-policy fallback and a quick diag checklist (1d).

carla (eng-runtime): I'll open the postmortem and link this thread. Adding logs/screenshot of p99 graphs.

alice (support): Closing note to customer: "We identified a transient configuration DB overload caused by an internal analytics job which slowed down routing and session lookups; we applied emergency fallback and restarted the routing service — the errors have stopped. We're doing follow-up work to prevent recurrence and will keep you posted." :thumbsup: 

ben (sre): adding monitoring dashboard + alert thresholds now. Will post links in the PM.

configdb-monitor-bot: INFO: Incident cleared at 10:28:45 UTC.

alice (support): Thanks everyone — great cross-team response. Leaving the thread open for the postmortem link.

oncall-manager (ops): Filing a formal incident ticket and assigning to carla.

carla (eng-runtime): Postmortem created: INC-200500 (link to internal doc). I'll ping when it's ready for review.

alice (support): ack.
